page.label: RISK ASSESSMENT
page.title: Recognize the signs of
page.subtitle: workplace bullying early.
page.description: This is not a diagnosis. This is a tool to visualize your situation. Answer honestly – no one else sees your answers.
page.answer_all_hint: Please answer all questions to see the result.
page.before_start_text: Breathe calmly. This is just one perspective on your situation. Answers are completely anonymous and stored only on this device.

questions.question: Do you doubt your ability to perform tasks that previously felt easy?
Do you feel like an outsider in your work community?
Do you have trouble sleeping because of work matters?
Do you feel your words are twisted or intentionally misunderstood?
Are you left uninvited to meetings or lunches?
Is your work constantly criticized without a clear reason?
Do you feel anxious on Sunday evenings or during your commute?
Do you have physical symptoms (headache, stomach pain) on workdays?
Does your supervisor or colleague avoid eye contact with you?
Does it feel like you are being watched or monitored?
Is your workload unreasonable compared to others?
Have work tasks been taken away from you without justification?
Is there gossip about you behind your back?
Do you feel 'on guard' all the time at work?
Have you been yelled or cursed at?
Are false rumors being spread about you?
Have you been forbidden from talking to others?
Have your opinions been repeatedly ignored?
Have you been called names or mocked?
Have you been threatened with dismissal?
Do you feel guilty about the situation?
Are you ashamed to tell your loved ones about the situation?
Do you feel you cannot trust anyone at work?
Have you considered resigning because of the situation?
Has your self-esteem dropped in your current job?
I experience success in my work.
My work community appreciates my contribution.
I feel safe at the workplace.
I can be myself at work.
I receive support from my supervisor when needed.
My tasks are clear and meaningful.
I have energy in my free time after the workday.
I trust my colleagues.
I dare to bring up grievances.
I feel heard.

results.alt_explanations: This could also be due to:

green.description: Your situation seems stable. The basic pillars of well-being at work are in order, even if there is normal stress in daily life. Continue setting boundaries and taking care of recovery.
green.disclaimer: This result is based on your answers. If you feel otherwise, trust your intuition.

yellow.description: There are noticeable stress factors which, if prolonged, can lead to burnout or deeper bullying cycles. Now is the right time to stop and examine the situation.

nextSteps.title: Start keeping a log
nextSteps.description: Write down concrete situations (what, where, when). This clarifies: is it a recurring pattern?

nextSteps.title: Talk to a trusted colleague
nextSteps.description: Ask 'have you noticed the same?' Reality checking is important.

yellow.disclaimer: Symptoms may indicate beginning workplace bullying or general burnout.

orange.description: There are serious warning signs in your situation. Your experiences suggest systematic inappropriate treatment or strong psychological load. Your ability to function is at risk.

nextSteps.title: Contact occupational health
nextSteps.description: Book an appointment with a work psychologist. Your symptoms are real and you need support.

nextSteps.title: Don't remain alone
nextSteps.description: Tell family or friends about the situation. Isolation is the goal of bullying – break it.

nextSteps.title: Clarify your legal protection
nextSteps.description: Check union membership and legal protection insurance.

orange.disclaimer: We recommend seeking professional help to clarify the situation.

red.description: You are in acute danger of burning out completely. Your work environment is toxic and your health is seriously threatened. The situation requires immediate actions to protect yourself.

nextSteps.title: See a doctor IMMEDIATELY
nextSteps.description: You likely need sick leave to detach from the situation and restore resources.

nextSteps.title: Prepare to leave
nextSteps.description: Your health is more important than this job. Find out the terms of resignation.

nextSteps.title: Make a report
nextSteps.description: Make an official report to occupational safety and the employer (in writing), if resources allow.
